Yes. I have played a lot of games, including others posted here. Playing WoW at the right time is still the best video game experience I've ever had.

There is absolutely nothing else like dropping yourself into a world that you know almost nothing about, and spending hours upon hours slowly working your way through a giant landscape. Newer MMOs like Guild Wars 2 are good at retaining newer players, but fail hard at having the same level of immersion due to loading screens in between zones and easy fast travel.

In the early days of WoW, you had to walk everywhere. You could easily take the wrong way and wander into a zone that was too high level for you and get stuck.

Instead of "the zone on the other side of those mountains" being up a path and through a portal, you often had to scan the mountains and follow twisted roads to find the right way through those mountains. Then, instead of getting a loading screen that tells you what zone you're headed into with a picture that sums it up, you would breach the crest of a hill and see the sprawling, weird landscape of a new zone laid out in front of you.

I remember heading to Thousand Needles for a quest, with no idea what I was to expect, and breaching the edge of a cliff to see dozens of plateaus laid out in front of me, with bridges connecting them, and dangerous creatures prowling between them.

Stumbling across world bosses you didn't know existed...finding temples that lead to dungeons or raids or just quest material...there was just no end to it for many many hours...days even.

The first thing I did when I reached top level in WoW was finish my explorer achievement. From there, once I'd been over the whole world once over, and been raiding for a while, it loses its charm. But at that point, I had put hundreds of days of playtime into the game and exploring everything I could about it...and there were still raids and dungeons I never got to see.

Truly an amazing experience that I wish I could go back and relive.

I believe most games can be more immersive if you take steps to prepare yourself for that kind of experience. Headphones are highly recommended first and foremost. My next tip is that you must intentionally slow yourself down. If you happen to play lots of twitch games and online shooters, the impulse to keep skipping cutscenes and mashing the A/X/etc. button to move through menus quickly can be hard to resist. Force yourself to stop that because it will break immersion faster than anything else. Take your time and try to appreciate minor details even in menus and credits. If you begin a game at this pace, you will be much more easily able to take the actual game at a slower more immersive pace. You must get inside the head of the character you play as, so role playing is necessary. Try to think as the character might think. React to situations as the character might react. Mostly though, I recommend stopping in every area you enter simply to soak in the atmosphere. Look at objects, look at the sky, look behind and under things, walk. Listen to the music, the environment, the sound effects.

If you play like this, I guarantee even a game like Duke Nukem Forever will be ten times more immersive and enjoyable.
